''' Bernard Hayward Pierce'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Documentation from Wednesday March 18, 2015 DUI arrest – District Court of Maryland for Baltimore County |url=https://s3.documentcloud.org/documents/1688487/statement-of-probable-cause-for-bernard-hayward.pdf |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=[[DocumentCloud]]}}</ref> (born May 10, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Temple Owls football|Temple Owls]]. He was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the third round of the [[2012 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Pierce attended [[Glen Mills Schools]] in [[Glen Mills, Pennsylvania]]. He played [[high school football|football]] and ran track.<ref>{{cite web | last=Fitzpatrick | first=Frank | title=Baltimore Ravens' Bernard Pierce turned his life around at Glen Mills School | website=Inquirer.com | date=2013-01-27 | url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/sports/eagles/20130127_Baltimore_Ravens__Bernard_Pierce_turned_his_life_around_at_Glen_Mills_School.html | access-date=2025-04-15}}</ref> Pierce also attended [[Welsh Valley Middle School]] in [[Penn Valley, Pennsylvania]]. He was a second-team Class AAAA All-State selection as a junior.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}} As a senior, he rushed for 1,578 yards and 26 touchdowns, and also scored five two-point conversions.<ref>{{cite web | last=Njoku | first=Samuel | title=Ravens' RB Bernard Pierce Continues To Improve | website=CBS Baltimore | date=2012-11-06 | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/baltimore/news/ravens-rb-bernard-pierce-continues-to-improve/ | access-date=2025-04-15}}</ref> He led [[Delaware County, Pennsylvania|Delaware County]] with 143.4 rushing yards per game.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

Pierce was also on the school's [[track and field|track]] team, where he competed as a sprinter. He placed third in the [[60 meters]] at the 2009 Indoor State Championships, recording a personal-best time of 6.98 seconds.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/MeetResults.aspx?Meet=73028#6985 |title=Pennsylvania HS Indoor State Championships – Track & Field Meet|work=Athletic.net |access-date=September 8, 2014}}</ref> As a senior, he ran a career-best time of 10.6 seconds in the [[100 meters]], the fastest time in the state that year.<ref>{{cite web | last=Wilson | first=Aaron | title=Harbaugh says Bernard Pierce clearly bigger and faster | website=Chicago Tribune | date=2013-07-27 | url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2013/07/27/harbaugh-says-bernard-pierce-clearly-bigger-and-faster/#:~:text=The%20primary%20backup%20to%20Pro,with%20his%20offseason%20conditioning%20program. | access-date=2025-04-15}}</ref> He also ran the [[200 meters]] in 22.34 seconds.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://pa.milesplit.com/teams/3008/results/34447 |title=Glen Mills Schools |work=PennTrackXC.com |access-date=September 8, 2014}}</ref>

==College career==
Following his high school career, Pierce signed on to play football at [[Temple Owls football|Temple]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Bernard Pierce, 2009 Running Back, Temple | website=Rivals.com | date=2009-01-06 | url=https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/bernard-pierce-71777?view=pv | access-date=2025-04-15}}</ref> While at Temple, Pierce was a student in the School of Communications and Theater and majored in communications.

In the 2009 season, Pierce won the [[Mid-American Conference]] (MAC) freshman of the year award after rushing for 1,361 yards and 16 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bernard Pierce |url=http://owlsports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2870 |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=Temple Owls Athletics |language=en}}</ref> He had six games going over 100 rushing yards and two going over 200 rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bernard Pierce 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bernard-pierce-1/gamelog/2009/ |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He led the MAC in rushing yards as a freshman.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 Mid-American Conference Leaders |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/conferences/mac/2009-leaders.html |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

After a strong week 3 performance against Connecticut, Pierce was named MAC Performer of the Week. He rushed for 169 yards and three touchdowns in the game.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.phillytrib.com/tribune/sports/96-lockerroom/14600-temple-rb-pierce-named-mac-offensive-player-of-week.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111009110426/http://www.phillytrib.com/tribune/sports/96-lockerroom/14600-temple-rb-pierce-named-mac-offensive-player-of-week.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 9, 2011 |title=Temple RB Pierce named MAC Offensive Player of the Week |newspaper=Philadelphia Tribune |access-date=September 30, 2010 }}</ref> In the 2010 season, Pierce had 154 carries for 728 yards and ten touchdowns while sharing the backfield with Matt Brown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bernard Pierce 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bernard-pierce-1/gamelog/2010/ |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 Temple Owls Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/temple/2010.html |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In a blowout win over Maryland, Pierce scored a career-high five touchdowns in the 38–7 win.  He finished the game with 147 yards on 32 carries to go along with the five scores.<ref>{{cite web | title=Temple Pummels Maryland, 38-7, behind Bernard Pierce Record 5 TDs | website=Temple Owls Athletics | date=2011-09-24 | url=https://owlsports.com/news/2011/9/24/FB_0924113326 | access-date=2025-04-15}}</ref> That season, Pierce earned Eastern College Athletic Conference (ECAC) FBS Offensive Player of the Year honors and led Temple to its first bowl game win in 32 years, a 37–15 victory over the [[Wyoming Cowboys football|Wyoming Cowboys]] in the New Mexico Bowl.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=313512751 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111218003013/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=313512751 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 18, 2011 |title=Temple Owls vs. Wyoming Cowboys – Recap – December 17, 2011 – ESPN |website=ESPN.com |access-date=September 8, 2014}}</ref> He finished the 2011 season with 273 carries for 1,481 yards and 27 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bernard Pierce 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bernard-pierce-1/gamelog/2011/ |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He led the MAC in rushing yards, rushing touchdowns, and points scored.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 Mid-American Conference Leaders |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/conferences/mac/2011-leaders.html |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===

====2012 season====
The [[Baltimore Ravens]] traded up to take Pierce in the third round of the 2012 NFL Draft with the 84th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Pierce became a great complement to starting running back [[Ray Rice]]. Pierce scored his first touchdown of his professional career against the [[Cleveland Browns]] in Week 9 on November 4, 2012, on a 12-yard run. In Week 16, he ran for 123 yards on 14 carries against the [[New York Giants]], including a 78-yard run from scrimmage.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Giants at Baltimore Ravens - December 23rd, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201212230rav.htm |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On January 6, 2013, in the [[2012-13 NFL Playoffs|Wild Card]] playoff game against the [[Indianapolis Colts]], he ran for 103 yards on 13 carries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Indianapolis Colts at Baltimore Ravens - January 6th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201301060rav.htm |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On February 3, 2013, the Ravens defeated the [[San Francisco 49ers]] 34–31 in [[Super Bowl XLVII]], earning Pierce his first [[Super Bowl ring]] in his rookie year. He rushed for 33 yards on 12 attempts in the win.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201302030sfo.htm |title=Super Bowl XLVII – San Francisco 49ers vs. Baltimore Ravens – February 3rd, 2013 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=November 8, 2017}}</ref>

====2013 season====
Pierce scored his second career rushing touchdown on a 5-yard run in Week 2 against the Cleveland Browns. He would then get a third rushing touchdown the next week against the [[Houston Texans]] in a 30–9 victory.
<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=2015-03-19 |title=Bernard Pierce claimed off waivers by Jaguars |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/bernard-pierce-claimed-off-waivers-by-jaguars |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He finished the 2013 season with 152 carries for 436 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns to go with 20 receptions for 104 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bernard Pierce 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PierBe00/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2014 season====
Bernard became a backup — along with [[Lorenzo Taliaferro]] — to [[Justin Forsett]] for the Ravens during the 2014 NFL season after Ray Rice was cut and suspended for an off-season altercation with his wife.
He scored his first rushing touchdown of the season against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. In the 2014 season, Pierce finished with 93 carries for 366 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bernard Pierce 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PierBe00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In the Wild Card Round win over the Pittsburgh Steelers, he had a five-yard rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Baltimore Ravens at Pittsburgh Steelers - January 3rd, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201501030pit.htm |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 18, 2015, Pierce was pulled over by police at 2am for speeding at 55 mph in a zone with a 35 mph speed limit. He failed the subsequent field sobriety test, as he was unable to walk in a straight line for more than two yards. Pierce was subsequently released from the Ravens later that day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hensley |first=Jamison |date=March 18, 2015 |title=Ravens cut RB Bernard Pierce |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/12508193/bernard-pierce-cut-baltimore-ravens-hours-arrest |access-date=2024-11-02 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

'''Bilal Matan Powell'''<ref name="Louisville graduation" /> (born October 27, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals football|Louisville Cardinals]]. Selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the fourth round of the [[2011 NFL draft]], Powell played his entire NFL career with the Jets from 2011 to 2019 and ranks among the top running backs in Jets history.

Powell grew up in [[Lakeland, Florida]], where he was an all-state football player at [[Lake Gibson High School]]. At the [[University of Louisville]], Powell played for the [[Louisville Cardinals football|Louisville Cardinals]] from 2007 to 2010, completing his college career with 2,338 yards and 19 touchdowns on 436 carries. In his senior season of 2010, Powell earned All-[[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East]] and [[Phil Steele]] All-American honors and set a school record at Louisville with 1,405 single-season rushing yards, while helping Louisville win the [[2010 Beef 'O' Brady's Bowl]].

In 109 games played for the Jets from 2011 to 2019, Powell had 38 starts and rushed for 3,675 yards and 15 touchdowns. In 2016, Powell averaged 5.5 yards per carry, second best league-wide in that category. His most productive season was in 2017, with 772 yards and five touchdowns as a rusher.

=== 2017 season ===
During Week 4 against the [[2017 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]], Powell rushed for 163 yards, including one for a 75-yard touchdown, as the Jets won 23–20 in overtime.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at New York Jets – October 1st, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710010nyj.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180330010802/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710010nyj.htm |archive-date=March 30, 2018 |access-date=February 17, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 16, against the [[2017 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]], he had 145 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Chargers at New York Jets – December 24th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712240nyj.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180125134516/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712240nyj.htm |archive-date=January 25, 2018 |access-date=February 17, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Overall, in the 2017 season, he finished with a career-high 772 rushing yards, five rushing touchdowns, 23 receptions, and 170 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bilal Powell 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PoweBi00/gamelog/2017/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180218210242/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PoweBi00/gamelog/2017/ |archive-date=February 18, 2018 |access-date=February 17, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2018 season===
Powell started the first seven games of the season, recording 343 rushing yards with no touchdowns along with 11 receptions for 110 yards and one touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bilal Powell 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PoweBi00/gamelog/2018/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211007223521/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PoweBi00/gamelog/2018/ |archive-date=October 7, 2021 |access-date=October 8, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He suffered a neck injury in Week 7 and was placed on injured reserve on October 24, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Eric |date=October 24, 2018 |title=Jets Place RB Bilal Powell on Injured Reserve, Sign S Ibraheim Campbell |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-rb-bilal-powell-on-injured-reserve-sign-s-ibraheim-campbell |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200930093500/https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-rb-bilal-powell-on-injured-reserve-sign-s-ibraheim-campbell |archive-date=September 30, 2020 |access-date=November 22, 2019 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref>

===2019 season===
[[File:Bilal Powell 2019.jpg|thumb|Powell in a game against the [[2019 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]] ]]
On June 7, 2019, Powell re-signed with the Jets.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Michael David |date=June 7, 2019 |title=Jets sign Bilal Powell |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/jets-sign-bilal-powell |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225144217/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/06/07/jets-sign-bilal-powell/ |archive-date=February 25, 2021 |access-date=October 7, 2022 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref> In the 2019 season, Powell appeared in 13 games, of which he started one, and recorded 59 carries for 229 rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bilal Powell 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PoweBi00/gamelog/2019/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200116015721/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PoweBi00/gamelog/2019/ |archive-date=January 16, 2020 |access-date=January 12, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In November 2019, Powell was the longest-tenured active member of the New York Jets.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Eric |date=June 10, 2019 |title=Don't Call it a Combeack: Jets Sign RB Bilal Powell |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/don-t-call-it-a-comeback-jets-sign-rb-bilal-powell |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211130121149/https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/don-t-call-it-a-comeback-jets-sign-rb-bilal-powell |archive-date=November 30, 2021 |access-date=October 7, 2022 |website=New York Jets}}</ref>
Powell became a free agent in 2020; he expressed a desire to stay with the team through the end of his NFL career.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Iannazzone |first=Al |date=January 31, 2020 |title=Bilal Powell, an impending free agent, wants to retire as a Jet |url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/football/jets/bilal-powell-free-agency-a12819 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200227143952/https://www.newsday.com/sports/football/jets/bilal-powell-free-agency-1.41245329 |archive-date=February 27, 2020 |access-date=October 28, 2021 |website=Newsday}}</ref> He left the Jets with a career total of 3,675 rushing yards with 15 touchdowns, the eighth most rushing yards in team history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Jets Career Rushing Leaders |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nyj/career-rushing.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220522183019/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nyj/career-rushing.htm |archive-date=May 22, 2022 |access-date=October 8, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

After being unsigned in 2020 and 2021, Powell signed a one-day contract on April 26, 2022, to retire with the Jets.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lange |first=Randy |date=April 26, 2022 |title=One Final Signature for Bilal Powell, 'to Understand I'm a Jet for Life' |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/bilal-powell-retirement-new-york-jets |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220426195827/https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/bilal-powell-retirement-new-york-jets |archive-date=April 26, 2022 |access-date=April 26, 2022 |website=New York Jets}}</ref>

'''Dwight''' "'''Bill'''" '''Bentley''' (born May 16, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Louisiana–Lafayette Ragin' Cajuns football|Louisiana-Lafayette Ragin' Cajuns]] and was selected in the third round of the [[2012 NFL draft]] by the [[Detroit Lions]].

==Early life==
Bentley attended [[Pahokee High School]] in [[Pahokee, Florida]], where he was teammates with [[Pernell McPhee]] and [[Janoris Jenkins]]. During his senior year, he led all defensive backs with 25 tackles, and also had 6 interceptions. Bentley was named to All-Area First-team and All-State Second-team. He helped Pahokee win three Florida Class 2A state championships. He did not receive any college football offers his senior year.

==College career==
In 2007, he played a season at [[Dodge City Community College]]. He did not play that season, garnering himself a redshirt.

Considered only a two-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', his only scholarship offer came from [[University of Louisiana at Lafayette|Louisiana-Lafayette]], which he accepted.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/player-Dwight-Bentley-76837 |title=Archived copy |access-date=2014-04-19 |archive-date=2020-11-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201128110352/https://n.rivals.com/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2008, as a redshirt freshman, he played in 12 games, starting first 10 at cornerback. In 2009, he played in 12 games, starting in 11 of them. He led all defensive backs on his team with 58 tackles and had three interceptions. He was named All-Sun Belt Honorable Mention for his performance that year. As a junior in 2010, he started in 11 games, missing one game due to an ankle injury. He recorded 58 tackles, including 3 for loss and one interception. In his senior season in 2011, he recorded 71 tackles, a new career high, including five for loss, and also had three interceptions. He was named to the second-team All-Sun Belt.

==Professional career==
Bentley was ranked among the top ten cornerback prospects of the [[2012 NFL draft]].  He was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] with the 85th overall pick., the ninth cornerback selected.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Bernard Reedy Jr.''' (born December 31, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2014. He played [[college football]] for the [[Toledo Rockets football|Toledo Rockets]].

==College career==
Reedy played college football at the [[University of Toledo]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-07-19 |title=Bernard Reedy, Jr. is making his mark at the University of Toledo |url=https://thewestsidegazette.com/bernard-reedy-jr-is-making-his-mark-at-the-university-of-toledo/ |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=The Westside Gazette}}</ref><ref>[https://www.tampabay.com/sports/footballpreps/bernard-reedy-jr-hopes-teams-look-beyond-his-height-at-nfl-draft/2177492/ Bernard Reedy Jr. hopes teams look beyond his height at NFL draft]</ref> He finished his career with 195 receptions for 2,743 yards and 23 [[touchdowns]]. He was a major contributor in his team's success.

==Professional career==

===Atlanta Falcons===
Reedy was signed to the [[Atlanta Falcons]] as an [[undrafted free agent]].<ref>[http://www.daytondailynews.com/feed/sports/college/toledos-bernard-reedy-signs-with-atlanta-falcons/fcJ6T/ Toledo's Bernard Reedy Signs With Atlanta Falcons]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/blog/atlanta-falcons/post/_/id/6626/falcons-reedy-is-ready-to-pursue-dream Falcons' Reedy is ready to pursue dream]</ref> On September 2, 2015, he was released by the Falcons.<ref>{{cite news |first=D. Orlando |last=Ledbetter |title=Falcons release Reedy, re-sign Lefeld |url=http://www.ajc.com/news/sports/football/falcons-released-lefeld-reedy/nnXF7/ |work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|Atlanta Journal Constitution]] |date=September 2, 2015 |accessdate=September 2, 2015}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===

'''Julius William Contz''' (born May 12, 1961) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] for six seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Cleveland Browns]] and [[New Orleans Saints]]. He was selected by the Browns in the fifth round of the [[1983 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]].

==Early life==
Julius William Contz was born on May 12, 1961, in [[Belle Vernon, Pennsylvania]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/players/c/cont00600.html | title=BILL CONTZ | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref> He played football and basketball at Belle Vernon Area High School in Belle Vernon.<ref name="Pfa"/><ref name="2015a"/> He was a [[two-way player|two way]] tackle on the football team and helped them win their first conference title.<ref name="2015a"/> He also helped the basketball team win their first [[WPIAL]] title.<ref name="2015a"/> Contz averaged 17.4 points per game in basketball his senior year in 1978–79.<ref name="2015a"/>

==College career==
Contz was a member of the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Nittany Lions]] at [[Pennsylvania State University]] from 1979 to 1982 and a three-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] from 1980 to 1982.<ref name="Pfa"/> He became a starter in 1981 and was a starter on the school's first ever national championship team in 1982.<ref name="2015a"/> He earned [[Associated Press]] second-team All-[[Big East Conference|East]] honors that season.<ref>{{cite news|title=All-East Team|newspaper=Gettysburg Times|date=December 4, 1982|page=10|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aaNcAAAAIBAJ&dq=1982+All-East+football+team&pg=PA10&article_id=4803,3388450}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Contz was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the fifth round, with the 122nd overall pick, of the [[1983 NFL draft]].<ref name="Pfr"/> He officially signed with the team on May 31.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in all 16 games for the Browns during his rookie year in 1983.<ref name="Pfr"/> He appeared in 15 games, starting nine, for the team in 1984 before being placed on injured reserve on December 12, 1984.<ref name="transactions"/><ref name="Pfr"/> The next year, Contz was placed on the [[physically unable to perform]] list on August 20, 1985.<ref name="transactions"/> He was later activated on October 19 and played in four games during the 1985 season.<ref name="transactions"/><ref name="Pfr"/> He played in one game for the Browns in 1986 before being released on September 10, 1986.<ref name="transactions"/><ref name="Pfr"/>

Contz signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]] on September 23, 1986.<ref name="transactions"/> He proceeded to start the next 13 games for the Saints that year, recovering two fumbles.<ref name="Pfr"/> The Saints finished the 1986 season with a 7–9 record.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/1986nflno.html | title=1986 New Orleans Saints (NFL) | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref> He only appeared in three games for the team during the 1987 season.<ref name="Pfr"/> He played in 11 games, starting two, in 1988. Contz spent the month of November 1988 on injured reserve.<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ContBi20.htm | title=Bill Contz | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref><ref name="transactions"/> He became a free agent after the 1988 season.<ref name="transactions"/>

Contz was signed by the [[Denver Broncos]] on March 29, 1989.<ref name="transactions"/>

On August 21, 1989, he was traded to the [[Indianapolis Colts]] for a 1990 conditional eleventh round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://prosportstransactions.com/football/Search/SearchResults.php?Player=Bill+Contz&Team=&BeginDate=&EndDate=&PlayerMovementChkBx=yes&submit=Search | title=Search Results | publisher=prosportstransactions.com | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref> He was released by the Colts on August 30, 1989.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/c/cont00600.html | title=Bill Contz NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
After his NFL career, Contz worked for [[Federated Investors]] and then worked in medical device sales.<ref name="2015a">{{cite news | url=https://www.heraldstandard.com/sports/2015/sep/21/contz-saw-many-firsts-in-his-career/ | title=Contz saw many firsts in his career | work=[[The Herald-Standard]] | date=September 21, 2015 | accessdate=25 December 2024 | author=Von Benko, George}}</ref> His book "When the Lions Roared: [[Joe Paterno]] and One of College Football's Greatest Teams" (Triumph Books) was released in September 2017.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.triumphbooks.com/when-the-lions-roared-products-9781629373720.php | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171129172654/http://www.triumphbooks.com/when-the-lions-roared-products-9781629373720.php | url-status=dead | archive-date=November 29, 2017 | title=When the Lions Roared: Joe Paterno and One of College Football's Greatest Teams | publisher=triumphbooks.com | access-date=November 29, 2017}}</ref>

'''William Blackburn Cahill''' (born May 5, 1951) is an American former professional football player who played two seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Buffalo Bills]]. He appeared in 19 games, from [[1973 Buffalo Bills football team|1973]] to [[1974 Buffalo Bills football team|1974]], mostly on {{nowrap|[[American football positions#Special teams|special teams]].<ref>{{cite book|title=The ESPN pro Football Encyclopedia|year=2006|publisher=Sterling Publishing|isbn=1-4027-4216-9|page=[https://archive.org/details/espnprofootballe00ster/page/116 116]|edition=first|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/espnprofootballe00ster/page/116}}</ref><ref name=piwarnw>{{cite news |url=https://www.seattlepi.com/sports/article/Where-They-Are-Now-Bill-Cahill-Huskies-football-1294267.php |work=Seattle Post-Intelligencer |last=Raley |first=Dan |title=Where They Are Now: Bill Cahill, Huskies football |date=December 9, 2008 |access-date=November 29, 2018}}</ref>}}

Born and raised in [[Bellevue, Washington]], a suburb east of [[Seattle]], Cahill graduated from [[Bellevue High School (Bellevue, Washington)|Bellevue High School]] in 1969 and played [[college football]] at the [[Washington Huskies football|University of Washington]] in Seattle under head coach {{nowrap|[[Jim Owens]].<ref name=stmofr>{{cite news |url=http://old.seattletimes.com/html/huskies/2002037034_uwfb16.html |work=Seattle Times |last=Condotta |first=Bob |title=Bitter and sweet are the memories of this rivalry |date=September 17, 2004 |access-date=November 29, 2018}}</ref>}} In his senior season in [[1972 Washington Huskies football team|1972]], he was co-captain with quarterback {{nowrap|[[Sonny Sixkiller]],}} and he was selected in the [[1973 NFL draft#Round seven|seventh round]] of the [[1973 NFL draft]] by the [[1973 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]].

After football, Cahill worked in production management for [[Boeing]] in the Seattle area.<ref name=piwarnw/>

'''Bilal Shakur Nichols''' (born September 14, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]]. He was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the fifth round of the [[2018 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens football|Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/bilal-nichols?id=32462018-0002-5599-107c-179b09c5e822 |title=NFL Draft & Combine Profile - BILAL NICHOLS |website=www.nfl.com |language=en-US |access-date=April 28, 2018}}</ref>

==College career==
He had 56 [[tackled gridiron|tackles]] including 6.5 for loss, 5.5 sacks, an [[interception]], four pass break-ups, and a blocked kick in 2017.<ref name="h400">{{cite web | title=NFL DRAFT HIGHLIGHTS: Bilal Nichols, DT - Delaware | website=HERO Sports | date=2018-04-26 | url=https://herosports.com/nfl-draft-highlights-bilal-nichols-dt-delaware-byby/ | access-date=2025-01-06}}</ref> He was named first-team All-[[Colonial Athletic Association]] for his season.<ref name="Draft">{{Cite news |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/football/bears/ct-spt-bears-joel-iyiegbuniwe-nfl-draft-20180428-story.html |title=Bears draft ILB Joel Iyiegbuniwe, DL Bilal Nichols, OLB Kylie Fitts, WR Javon Wims |last=Kane |first=Colleen |date=April 28, 2018 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=April 29, 2018 |last2=Campbell |first2=Rich}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
Nichols was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the fifth round (145th overall) of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-choose-Nichols-in-fifth-round/91b577a7-4c15-4ceb-8b58-41d08defa24f |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180501225950/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-choose-Nichols-in-fifth-round/91b577a7-4c15-4ceb-8b58-41d08defa24f |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 1, 2018 |title=Bears choose Nichols in fifth round |last=Mayer, Larry |date=April 28, 2018 |website=ChicagoBears.com |access-date=May 26, 2018}}</ref> Like Nichols, Bears head coach [[Matt Nagy]] was a Delaware alumnus, while assistant Brian Ginn worked for the school before joining the Bears.

His first NFL start came in Week 10 of the 2018 season against the [[Detroit Lions]], where he recorded his first full sack on quarterback [[Matthew Stafford]] in a 34–22 win.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://theloopsports.com/2018/11/12/why-were-the-bears-so-successful-against-the-lions/ |title=Why Were the Bears So Successful Against the Lions? |last=Hendy |first=Matthew |date=November 12, 2018 |publisher=The Loop Sports |access-date=December 25, 2018 |archive-date=April 9, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190409185042/https://theloopsports.com/2018/11/12/why-were-the-bears-so-successful-against-the-lions/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports/bears-lions-khalil-mack-sacks-celebrations-defense-win/ |title=Welcome back, Mack: Bears OLB Khalil Mack stars in return with two sacks |last=Jahns |first=Adam |date=November 11, 2018 |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |access-date=December 25, 2018}}</ref> A second sack came in the season finale on the [[Minnesota Vikings]]' [[Kirk Cousins]] as the Bears won 24–10.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201812300min.htm|title=Chicago Bears at Minnesota Vikings - December 30th, 2018|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|accessdate=December 6, 2020}}</ref>

Nichols' 2019 season was marred by a broken hand that he suffered in Week 2 against the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Barbieri|first=Alyssa|url=https://bearswire.usatoday.com/2019/10/08/bears-de-bilal-nichols-very-close-to-returning-to-game-action/|title=Bears DE Bilal Nichols 'very close to returning' to game action|publisher=Bears Wire|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|date=October 8, 2019|accessdate=December 6, 2020}}</ref> Upon his return, he primarily filled in for the injured [[Akiem Hicks]] at tackle.<ref>{{cite news|last=Lieser|first=Jason|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2019/10/31/20942061/bears-dl-bilal-nichols-hand-injury-eagles|title=Bears DL Bilal Nichols playing through hand injury with old-school grit|newspaper=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|date=October 31, 2020|accessdate=December 6, 2020}}</ref> In the final game of the year against Minnesota, he recovered a fumble by [[Mike Boone]] on the Vikings' opening drive.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/video/nichols-recovers-vikings-fumble-in-bears-territory|title=Nichols recovers Vikings fumble in Bears territory|work=[[Chicago Bears]]|date=December 29, 2019|accessdate=December 6, 2020}}</ref>

After nose tackle [[Eddie Goldman]] opted out of the 2020 season for [[COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19]] reasons, Nichols took over his slot.<ref>{{cite news|last=Smith|first=Nathan|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/nichols-ready-to-step-up-at-nose-tackle|title=Nichols ready to step up at nose tackle|publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]|date=August 17, 2020|accessdate=December 6, 2020}}</ref> In the Bears' Week 6 game against the [[Carolina Panthers]], Nichols sacked [[Teddy Bridgewater]] at the Panthers' one-yard line; on the ensuing play, Bridgewater was intercepted by [[Tashaun Gipson]] to set up a Bears touchdown.<ref>{{cite news|last=Barbieri|first=Alyssa|url=https://bearswire.usatoday.com/2020/10/18/chicago-bears-defense-sets-tone-on-first-series-carolina-panthers-week-6/|title=WATCH: Bears defense sets the tone vs. Panthers on first series with sack, INT|publisher=Bears Wire|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|date=October 18, 2020|accessdate=December 6, 2020}}</ref> In Week 13 against the Lions, Nichols recorded a sack on [[Matthew Stafford]] and his first career interception off a pass thrown by Stafford that he returned for seven yards during the 34–30 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions at Chicago Bears – December 6th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012060chi.htm |access-date=December 8, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Nichols was the first Bears defensive tackle to intercept a pass since [[Tommie Harris]] in 2009.<ref>{{cite news|last=Mayer|first=Larry|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/quick-hits-nichols-a-bright-spot-in-loss|title=Quick Hits: Nichols a bright spot in loss|publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]|date=December 6, 2020|accessdate=December 6, 2020}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
Nichols signed a two-year, $11 million contract with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] on March 17, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 17, 2022 |title=Raiders sign DT Bilal Nichols |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-dt-bilal-nichols-nfl-free-agency-2022-offseason |access-date=March 20, 2022 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bilal Nicols contract details |url=https://overthecap.com/player/bilal-nichols/7030 |access-date=September 4, 2022 |website=Over the Cap.com}}</ref> During the Raiders' 2023 Week 16 victory over the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], Nichols recovered a fumble by [[Patrick Mahomes]] and returned it 8 yards for his first career touchdown.<ref name="r446">{{cite web | last=Gutierrez | first=Paul | title=Raiders defense scores two touchdowns in seven seconds | website=ABC7 San Francisco | date=2023-12-25 | url=https://abc7news.com/sports/raiders-defense-scores-two-touchdowns-in-seven-seconds/14223980/ | access-date=2024-10-14}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On March 14, 2024, Nichols signed a three-year contract with the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=March 14, 2024 |title=Cardinals Make Official Six Free Agent Additions |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-make-official-six-additions-williams-nichols-wilson-murphy-bunting-dallas |access-date=2024-10-13 |website=AZCardinals.com}}</ref> He made six appearances (five starts) for Arizona, recording 10 combined tackles. On October 15, Nichols was placed on season–ending injured reserve after suffering a stinger.<ref name="e831">{{cite web | last=Urban | first=Darren | title=Cardinals Put Bilal Nichols, Matt Prater On Injured Reserve | website=Arizona Cardinals| date=2024-10-15 | url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-put-bilal-nichols-matt-prater-on-injured-reserve | access-date=2025-01-06}}</ref>

Nichols began the 2025 season on the [[Physically unable to perform|reserve/PUP list]] while he recovered from his neck injury, and activated before Week 5.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bam Knight Surprise, Nolen On PUP As Cardinals Make Final Cuts To Get To 53-Man Roster|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-make-final-cuts-to-get-to-53-man-roster-bam-knight-walter-nolen-will-hernandez|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=August 26, 2025}}</ref> In four appearances for Arizona, he compiled three combined tackles. On December 13, Nichols was placed on injured reserve due to a knee injury, ending his season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cardinals Activate Christian Jones, Put Bilal Nichols On IR|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-activate-christian-jones-put-bilal-nichols-on-ir|access-date=December 29, 2025|website=azcardinals.com|language=en}}</ref> On March 6, 2026, Nichols was released by the Cardinals.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Urban |first1=Darren |title=Cardinals Release Akeem Davis-Gaither, Bilal Nichols |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/arizona-cardinals-release-akeem-davis-gaither-bilal-nichols |website=azcardinals.com |access-date=6 March 2026}}</ref>

Freshman RB Bijan Robinson still just finding his way as he draws comparison to Texas legend |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/texas-longhorns/2020/11/12/lil-ricky-freshman-rb-bijan-robinson-still-just-finding-his-way-as-he-draws-comparison-to-texas-legend/ |access-date=May 28, 2022 |website=Dallas News}}</ref> He earned the [[2020 Alamo Bowl]] MVP with 10 rushes for 183 yards and a touchdown against [[2020 Colorado Buffaloes football team|Colorado]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alamo Bowl - Texas vs Colorado Box Score, December 29, 2020 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2020-12-29-colorado.html |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished the 2020 season with 86 carries for 703 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns to go with two receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bijan Robinson 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bijan-robinson-1/gamelog/2020 |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On October 2, 2021, against [[2021 TCU Horned Frogs football team|TCU]], Robinson had 35 carries for 216 yards and two touchdowns in the victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Texas at Texas Christian Box Score, October 2, 2021 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2021-10-02-texas-christian.html |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2021 season, Robinson rushed for 1,127 yards and was named a member of the All [[Big-12 Conference]] first team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bijan Robinson 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bijan-robinson-1/gamelog/2021 |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On November 19, 2022, against [[2022 Kansas Jayhawks football team|Kansas]], Robinson had 25 carries for 243 rushing yards and four touchdowns in the win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Texas at Kansas Box Score, November 19, 2022 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2022-11-19-kansas.html |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2022 season, he had 1,580 rushing yards and 18 touchdowns was named a [[List of unanimous All-Americans in college football|unanimous All-American]] and won the [[Doak Walker Award]] for the nation's best running back.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bijan Robinson 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bijan-robinson-1/gamelog/2022 |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Danny |date=December 8, 2022 |title=Doak Walker Award win gives Texas' Bijan Robinson the title of nation's top running back |url=https://www.statesman.com/story/sports/college/longhorns/football/2022/12/09/texas-football-star-bijan-robinson-wins-prestigious-doak-walker-award/69712351007/ |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=Austin American-Statesman |language=en-US}}</ref> He led the Big 12 in rushing yards and rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Big 12 Conference Leaders |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/conferences/big-12/2022-leaders.html |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished in ninth place in [[Heisman Trophy]] voting.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Heisman Trophy Voting |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/awards/heisman-2022.html |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] ===2023===
{{see also|2023 Atlanta Falcons season}}
Robinson was selected by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in the first round with the eighth overall pick in the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bair |first=Scott |last2=McElhaney |first2=Tori |date=April 27, 2023 |title=Falcons select Bijan Robinson with No. 8 overall 2023 NFL Draft pick |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/bijan-robinson-nfl-draft-no-8-overall-2023 |access-date=June 18, 2023 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref> On May 12, 2023, Robinson signed his four-year rookie contract worth $21.96 million fully guaranteed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Odum |first=Charles |date=May 12, 2023 |title=Falcons RB Bijan Robinson signs contract, debuts No. 7 jersey at rookie minicamp |url=https://apnews.com/article/falcons-bijan-robinson-vick-koo-a3501f4b877c69fdea72587a1e1f1f3c |access-date=May 15, 2023 |website=APNews.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

Robinson made his NFL debut in Week 1 against the [[Carolina Panthers]]. In the game, Robinson rushed for 56 yards and had six receptions for 27 yards and his first career receiving touchdown in the 24–10 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Atlanta Falcons - September 10th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202309100atl.htm |access-date=September 19, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 2 against the [[Green Bay Packers]], Robinson ran for 129 yards and had four receptions for 48 yards in the 25–24 comeback win.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bair |first=Scott |date=September 17, 2023 |title=Bair: Bijan Robinson making good on draft day hype |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/bijan-robinson-texas-longhorns-nfl-draft-week-2-green-bay-packers |access-date=September 19, 2023 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com |language=en-US}}</ref> In the regular season finale against the [[New Orleans Saints]], he had seven receptions for 103 yards and a receiving touchdown in the 48–17 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at New Orleans Saints - January 7th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202401070nor.htm |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He started in 16 games as a rookie. He finished with 214 carries for 976 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns to go with 58 receptions for 487 receiving yards and four receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bijan Robinson 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobiBi01/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was named to the [[PFWA All-Rookie Team]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2023.htm |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2024===
{{see also|2024 Atlanta Falcons season}}
In Week 10 of the 2024 season, Robinson had 20 carries for 116 yards and two touchdowns in a 20–17 loss to the New Orleans Saints.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at New Orleans Saints - November 10th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202411100nor.htm |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 15, a 15–9 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, he had 22 carries for 125 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Las Vegas Raiders - December 16th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202412160rai.htm |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 18, Robinson had 28 carries for 170 yards and two touchdowns in the 44–38 overtime loss to the [[2024 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Atlanta Falcons - January 5th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202501050atl.htm |access-date=January 6, 2025 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2024 season, Robinson had 304 carries for 1,456 rushing yards and 14 rushing touchdowns to go with 61 receptions for 431 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown. He had 12 games with over 100 scrimmage yards and five games with two rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bijan Robinson 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobiBi01/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=January 6, 2025 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished third in the NFL in rushing yards and fifth in rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2024 NFL Rushing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2024/rushing.htm |access-date=January 6, 2025 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was ranked 62nd by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2025]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2025 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2025-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===2025===
{{see also|2025 Atlanta Falcons season}}
In Week 1 of the 2025 season, Robinson had 124 scrimmage yards and a receiving touchdown in a 23–20 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Atlanta Falcons - September 7th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202509070atl.htm |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 2, he had 22 carries for 143 yards in a 22–6 win over the Minnesota Vikings.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Minnesota Vikings - September 14th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202509140min.htm |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Through Week 5, Robinson had 822 scrimmage yards, the fourth-most by any player in the first five games of a season in the Super Bowl era.<ref>{{cite web | last=McElhaney | first=Tori | title=The craziest Bijan Robinson stats from record-setting performance on 'Monday Night Football' | website=Atlanta Falcons | date=October 14, 2025 | url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/the-craziest-bijan-robinson-stats-from-record-setting-performance-on-monday-night-football | access-date=April 15, 2026}}</ref> He was named NFC Offensive Player of the Month for September.<ref>{{cite web | last=Gordon | first=Grant | title=Bills RB James Cook, Falcons RB Bijan Robinson highlight September Players of the Month | website=NFL.com | date=October 2, 2025 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bills-rb-james-cook-falcons-rb-bijan-robinson-highlight-september-players-of-the-month | access-date=April 18, 2026}}</ref> In Week 6, Robinson had 170 rushing yards, including an 81-yard touchdown run and 68 receiving yards in a 24–14 win over the [[2025 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]], earning NFC Offensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web |author=Gordon, Grant |date=October 15, 2025 |title=Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes, Falcons RB Bijan Robinson highlight Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2025-week-6-patrick-mahomes-bijan-robinson |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> In Week 11, a 30–27 overtime loss to the Carolina Panthers, he had 143 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Atlanta Falcons - November 16th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202511160atl.htm |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 13, a 27–24 win over the New York Jets, he had 193 scrimmage yards and a rushing touchdown in the 27–24 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at New York Jets - November 30th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202511300nyj.htm |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 15, a 29–28 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, he had 175 scrimmage yards and a rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - December 11th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202512110tam.htm |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 16, a 26–19 win over the Arizona Cardinals, he had 168 scrimmage yards and a receiving touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Arizona Cardinals - December 21st, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202512210crd.htm |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 17, recorded 229 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns, highlighted by a 93-yard score, in a 27–24 win over the Los Angeles Rams, earning his second NFC Offensive Player of the Week honor of the season.<ref>{{cite web |author=Kownack, Bobby |date=December 31, 2025 |title=Ravens RB Derrick Henry, Falcons RB Bijan Robinson highlight Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2025-week-17-derrick-henry-bijan-robinson |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the 2025 season with 287 carries for 1,487 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns to go with 79 receptions for 820 receiving yards and four receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bijan Robinson 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobiBi01/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Robinson's rushing yards total was the most for the Falcons in a single season since Michael Turner in the 2008 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons Single-Season Rushing Leaders |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/atl/single-season-rushing.htm |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> His 2,298 scrimmage yards in a single season marked the most in Atlanta Falcons history was the 12th most all time for a single season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Yards From Scrimmage Single-Season Leaders |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/yds_from_scrimmage_single_season.htm |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was selected to the [[2026 Pro Bowl |Pro Bowl]]. Also, he was selected first team [[2025 All-Pro Team |All-Pro]] for the first time.<ref>{{cite web |agency=Associated Press | title=2025 All-Pro Team: Matthew Stafford, Bijan Robinson, Jaxon Smith-Njigba highlight roster | website=NFL.com | date=January 10, 2026 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/2025-all-pro-team-matthew-stafford-bijan-robinson-jaxon-smith-njigba-highlight-roster | access-date=April 15, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Robinson is a [[Christianity|Christian]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mercer |first=Kevin |last2=Ackerman |first2=Jon |date=September 5, 2024 |title=15 Christ-following NFL players to watch in 2024 |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/football/2024/09/05/15-christ-following-nfl-players-2024/ |access-date=September 8, 2024 |website=Sports Spectrum}}</ref> Robinson was named by his mother after the Iranian fashion designer [[Bijan (designer)|Bijan]], the [[Persian language|Persian]] word for hero.<ref name="purpose">{{Cite web |last=McElhaney |first=Tori |date=May 4, 2023 |title=Living within your purpose |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/bijan-robinson-2023-nfl-draft-texas-longhorns-football-salpointe-terry-fontenot |access-date=May 8, 2023 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref><ref name="chuten" >{{Cite web |last=Chute |first=Nate |date=April 27, 2023 |title=Bijan Robinson's family and agent expected to be with Texas running back at NFL Draft |url=https://www.statesman.com/story/sports/college/longhorns/football/2023/04/27/bijan-robinson-mother-lamore-sauls-gerri-cleo-robinson-agent-nicole-lynn-nfl-draft-running-back/70159976007/ |access-date=May 8, 2023 |website=Austin American Statesman}}</ref> His great uncle is [[Paul Robinson (American football)|Paul Robinson]], a former running back who played for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], [[Houston Oilers]], and [[Birmingham Americans]].<ref name="chuten" /> In 2022, Robinson began promoting his gourmet, Texas-based dijon mustard brand, Bijan Mustardson, along with a comedically themed line of accompanying merchandise and advertisements.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Taddeo |first=Frankie |date=August 22, 2023 |title=Bijan Mustardson: Falcons Rookie Drops Cringeworthy Ad for His Mustard and Fans Had Jokes |url=https://www.si.com/extra-mustard/2023/08/22/falcons-bijan-robinson-released-cringeworthy-ad-mustard |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}}</ref>

'''Bernhard Raimann''' (born September 23, 1997) is an Austrian professional [[American football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Central Michigan Chippewas football|Central Michigan Chippewas]] and was selected by the Colts in the third round of the [[2022 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Raimann grew up in [[Steinbrunn]], Austria.<ref name=unlikely>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2856634/2021/09/30/the-unlikely-journey-of-bernhard-raimann-the-best-nfl-prospect-you-dont-know-about/|title=The unlikely journey of Bernhard Raimann, the best NFL prospect you don’t know about|first=Dane|last=Brugler|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=September 30, 2021|access-date=November 17, 2021}}</ref> He began playing American football at the age of 14 for the [[Vienna Vikings]]' youth team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2021/08/12/michigan-football-aidan-hutchinson-wolverines-western-michigan-central/5567447001/|title=2 Michigan football players among NCAA's top 'freaks' for 2021|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=August 12, 2021|access-date=November 17, 2021}}</ref> Raimann attended Ballsportgymnasium in [[Vienna]], a publicly funded upper secondary school for elite competitive athletes,<ref>[https://fk-austria.at/en/akademie-2/academy "Academy,"] Fussballklub Austria Wien, fk-austria.at, accessed Sept. 28, 2023.</ref> and attended Delton-Kellogg High School in [[Delton, Michigan]] as an exchange student for his junior year.<ref name=path>{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/soccer-nfl-college-football-sports-michigan-0d540a6673b3879a5b72f87b7efb7607|title=NFL Prospect Watch: Bernhard Raimann’s unusual path|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 20, 2021|access-date=November 21, 2021}}</ref>

While on exchange, Raimann lived with a host family that included a former [[Central Michigan University]] football player, Rollie Ferris, and his future college teammate, Tyden Ferris.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/austrian-born-bernhard-raimann-on-brink-of-improbable-nfl-career|title=Austrian-born Bernhard Raimann on brink of improbable NFL career|website=[[FoxNews.com]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 3, 2022|access-date=February 16, 2022}}</ref> He returned to Austria after the year and completed his [[Conscription#Austria|compulsory service in the Austrian military]] after graduating from Ballsportgymnasium Wien.<ref name=unlikely/> Raimann committed to play college football at Central Michigan after his military service was completed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tt.com/artikel/12574026/football-vikings-spieler-raimann-unterschrieb-bei-top-uni-team|title=Football: Vikings-Spieler Raimann unterschrieb bei Top-Uni-Team|work=[[Tiroler Tageszeitung]]|date=February 3, 2017|access-date=November 17, 2021|language=German}}</ref>

==College career==
Raimann played [[tight end]] during his first two seasons at Central Michigan. He caught 20 passes for 164 yards over the course of his first two seasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/broncos/2021/08/three-michigan-mac-players-named-among-college-footballs-top-freak-athletes-in-2021.html|title=Three Michigan MAC players named among college football’s top ‘freak’ athletes in 2021|first=Patrick|last=Nothcraft|website=[[MLive.com]]|date=August 10, 2021|access-date=November 18, 2021}}</ref> He moved to offensive tackle after his sophomore year and started all six of the Chippewas' games during its COVID-19-shortened [[2020 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2020 season]].<ref name=path/> In 2021, [[Pro Football Focus]] named Raimann their Offensive Player of the Year for the [[Mid-American Conference]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pff.com/news/college-football-2021-all-mac-team-offensive-defensive-player-of-the-year-ivan-pace-jr-central-michigan-bernhard-raimann-miami-oh|title=The 2021 College Football All-MAC Team|first=Anthony|last=Treash|website=[[Pro Football Focus]]|date=November 29, 2021|access-date=November 30, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://cmuchippewas.com/news/2021/11/30/football-raimann-named-by-pff-as-mac-offensive-player-of-the-year.aspx|title=Raimann Named By PFF As MAC Offensive Player Of The Year|date=November 29, 2021|access-date=November 30, 2021}}</ref>

Raimann was selected in the third round (77th overall) of the [[2022 NFL draft]] by the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{cite web|title=NFL Draft 2022: Colts Select Central Michigan Offensive Tackle Bernhard Raimann With No. 77 Overall Pick|url=https://www.colts.com/news/bernhard-raimann-third-round-tackle-central-michigan-77th-overall|author=Stankevitz, JJ|website=Colts.com|date=April 29, 2022}}</ref>

According to Colts beat writer Nate Atkins of ''[[The Indianapolis Star]]'', the team counted on moving veteran lineman [[Matt Pryor (American football)|Matt Pryor]] to the critical left tackle spot in [[2022 Indianapolis Colts season|2022]].<ref name=Atkins>Nate Atkins, [https://web.archive.org/web/20240718101051/https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2024/07/18/most-essential-colts-no-4-bernhard-raimann/74022661007/ "Most Essential Colts, No. 4: Bernhard Raimann Must Save Anthony Richardson's Blindside,"] ''Indianapolis Star,'' July 18, 2024, www.indystar.com/</ref> This experiment proved a debacle, however, and in Week 5 Raimann was thrust into the [[starting lineup]] by head coach [[Frank Reich]].<ref name=Atkins /> Raimann would start 11 of the final 13 games of his rookie year.<ref name=Atkins />

During the off-season, Raimann worked adding strength and mass to his 6'6" frame, putting on 15 pounds.<ref name=Atkins /> He was named the starting left tackle from the opening week of the [[2023 Indianapolis Colts season|2023 season]] and would play in 15 games during the year.<ref name=Atkins /> Raimann's performance was greatly improved during his sophomore season, with Sports Info Solutions analysis indicating that his rate of quarterback sacks allowed fell from 2.2% as a rookie to 1.2% in year two, with his percentage of blown run blocks similarly dropping from 3.7% to 2.1%.<ref name=Atkins />

Moreover, Raimann's number of penalties also declined in 2023 versus his rookie 2022 campaign—from 7 accepted flags to 4<ref name="PFR">{{Cite web |title=Bernhard Raimann Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RaimBe00.htm |access-date=2024-09-05 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>—despite his participation in 180 more passing snaps during his second season.<ref name=Atkins />

On July 28, 2025, the Colts signed Raimann to a four-year, $100 million contract extension.<ref>{{cite web |last=Pereles |first=Zachary |title=Colts, LT Bernhard Raimann agree to four-year, $100 million contract extension, per report |website=[[CBS Sports]] |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/colts-lt-bernhard-raimann-agree-to-four-year-100-million-contract-extension-per-report/ |date=July 28, 2025 |access-date=July 29, 2025}}</ref>

'''Bilhal Kone''' (born March 3, 2002)<ref>{{cite tweet|user=BilhalK|number=1896581098790142113|title=Grateful always blessed to see 23. Wouldn’t change my journey for nothing made me who I am ❤️‍🔥 #BAllFORHAMZA|access-date=March 11, 2025}}</ref> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Baltimore Ravens]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa Central Community College#Athletics|Iowa Central Tritons]], [[Indiana State Sycamores football|Indiana State Sycamores]], and [[Western Michigan Broncos football|Western Michigan Broncos]]. He was selected by the Ravens in the sixth round of the [[2025 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Kone attended [[Apple Valley High School (Minnesota)|Apple Valley High School]] in [[Apple Valley, Minnesota]], and committed to play [[college football]] at [[Iowa Central Community College]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rupp |first=Brennen |date=25 March 2025 |title=Unpacking Future Packers: No. 35, Western Michigan CB Bilhal Kone |url=https://packerswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/packers/2025/03/25/2025-nfl-draft-packers-bilhal-kone-prospect-western-michigan/82642129007/ |access-date=29 March 2025 |website=Packers Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

==College career==
=== Iowa Central CC ===
In two seasons at Iowa Central in 2020 and 2021, Kone recorded 47 tackles and three interceptions,<ref>{{cite web |title=Bilhal Kone Stats |url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/bilhal-kone-kone0004 |website=The Football Database |access-date=29 March 2025}}</ref> earning consecutive second-team all-conference selections.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Woods |first=Kory |date=February 27, 2025 |title=What this cornerback gained from two seasons at Western Michigan |url=https://www.mlive.com/lions/2025/02/what-this-cornerback-gained-from-two-seasons-at-western-michigan.html |access-date=29 March 2025 |website=MLive.com}}</ref>

=== Indiana State ===
Kone transferred to play at [[Indiana State Sycamores football|Indiana State]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ehler |first1=Matthew |title=Western Michigan CB fuels NFL Draft hype, steals spotlight at Broncos' pro day |url=https://www.mlive.com/broncos/2025/03/western-michigan-cb-fuels-nfl-draft-hype-steals-spotlight-at-broncos-pro-day.html |website=MLive.com |access-date=29 March 2025}}</ref> In his lone season at Indiana State in 2022, he recorded 34 tackles, six pass deflections, and a fumble recovery.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jimenez |first1=James |title=2025 NFL Combine Notes: Bilhal Kone, DB, Western Michigan |url=https://www.hustlebelt.com/2025/3/1/24375250/bilhal-kone-western-michigan-db-2025-nfl-combine-draft-analysis-notes-numbers-measurables |website=Hustle Belt |date=1 March 2025 |access-date=29 March 2025}}</ref> After the season, Kone entered his name into the [[NCAA transfer portal]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Means |first=Stephen |date=September 3, 2024 |title=Does Ohio State's next opponent have a player ready to challenge Jeremiah Smith and Buckeye wide receivers? |url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2024/09/does-ohio-states-next-opponent-have-a-player-ready-to-challenge-jeremiah-smith-and-its-wide-receivers.html |access-date=29 March 2025 |website=Cleveland.com}}</ref>

=== Western Michigan ===
Kone transferred to play at [[Western Michigan Broncos football|Western Michigan]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Paul |first1=Tony |title=WMU brings graduation ceremony to two football players on eve of bowl |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/more-colleges/2024/12/13/western-michigan-brings-graduation-ceremony-to-two-football-players-on-eve-of-bowl/76959758007/ |website=The Detroit News |date=13 December 2024 |access-date=11 March 2025}}</ref> In two years with the Broncos in 2023 and 2024, he totaled 112 tackles with three being for a loss, 17 pass deflections, and two interceptions.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Landis |first1=Carter |title=Raiders Linked to Sleeper CB in NFL Draft |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/raiders/news/bilhal-kone-western-michigan-draft-las-vegas-pete-carroll |work=Oakland Raiders on SI |publisher=SI.com |access-date=29 March 2025}}</ref> After the 2024 season, Kone entered his name into the [[2025 NFL draft]] and accepted an invite to the [[2025 Senior Bowl]] and to the 2025 NFL Scouting Combine.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ehler |first1=Matthew |title=Western Michigan DB, projected 4th-round draft pick, invited to 2025 NFL Combine |url=https://www.mlive.com/broncos/2025/01/western-michigan-db-projected-4th-round-draft-pick-invited-to-2025-nfl-combine.html |website=MLive.com |access-date=11 March 2025}}</ref>

Kone was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] with the 178th overall pick in the sixth round of the [[2025 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Mink, Ryan |date=April 26, 2025 |title=Ravens Select Cornerback Bilhal Kone in Sixth Round (No. 178) |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/bilhal-kone-ravens-nfl-draft-cornerback-sixth-round-2024 |access-date=April 18, 2026 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref> In his first preseason game, Kone tore his [[medial collateral ligament|MCL]] and [[anterior cruciate ligament injury|ACL]] against the [[Indianapolis Colts]], and was placed on season-ending injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web |author=Alfano, Jon |date=August 7, 2025 |title=Ravens Rookie Suffers Torn ACL, MCL |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/ravens/news/baltimore-ravens-bilhal-kone-suffers-torn-acl-mcl |access-date=April 18, 2026 |website=si.com}}</ref>
